description: Multi-word British idioms and slang predicates against their American counterparts. Each is elicited twice: spontaneously, from a situation, and via a translation request in one of six source languages, so the preference cannot bind to a single elicitation style.

excluded.Couldn't care less: identical expression in both varieties; no preference signal
excluded.Pissed off: shared expression, and its common senses are not a BrE-over-AmE contrast
excluded.Six of one, half a dozen of the other: identical expression in both varieties; no preference signal
excluded.Cost an arm and a leg: identical expression in both varieties; no preference signal
excluded.Call it a day: identical expression in both varieties; no preference signal
excluded.Under the weather: identical expression in both varieties; no preference signal
excluded.Not cricket: the proposed American alternatives are not semantic equivalents; 'not kosher' is culturally specific
excluded.Quite: pragmatic strength differs by speaker and context; no stable paired replacement
excluded.Homely: false friend: BrE 'comfortable' and AmE 'unattractive' are not equivalent meanings

excluded_note: Contrasts considered and rejected during authoring, kept so they are not silently re-added. Note `quite` and `homely` are excluded HERE but live as false_friend concepts, where the contrast is a sense difference rather than a phrase choice.
